subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should LanceDB memory solve this issue now by exposing exact deletion UUIDs in `memory_recall` visible content, or should the selector gap wait for the broader memory lifecycle contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract affects model-visible identifiers, exact deletion UX, and how this narrow repair relates to future tombstone/supersede/conflict semantics.

options.title: Expose recall UUIDs now
options.body: Add full deletable UUIDs to `memory_recall` visible content with focused regression coverage, leaving replacement and tombstone semantics to the Memory MVP tracker.

options.title: Route everything through Memory MVP
options.body: Defer the selector repair until maintainers settle the broader review, edit, forget, tombstone, and conflict-resolution design.

options.title: Choose another selector UX
options.body: Define a scoped deletion selector or list command instead of exposing UUIDs directly in recall output.

recommendation.title: Expose recall UUIDs now
recommendation.body: Add full deletable UUIDs to `memory_recall` visible content with focused regression coverage, leaving replacement and tombstone semantics to the Memory MVP tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent integration and memory/storage history make this the best available routing candidate for the product-contract choice.
